Text.Text: Alpha Rhythm. You found the true beat and you're keeping it, on your own now. Preserve doesn't need me tapping it out for you anymore. Go make some music.

Listen. Hear that? Off, just slightly, coming from past the tree line. That's the preserve, out of time with itself. You're out of time too, your own beast isn't following your beat yet. Come back when it is.

There it is again, that wrong beat. The pit-breeders who bought into the Tarn Jungle Preserve drove its kinrath to a rhythm that isn't theirs, then ran when the packs turned. The kinrath still keep that beat. Go into the preserve on Dathomir. Put down six of the Young Kinrath, the pack nearest the gate. Any Young Kinrath will do, the whole preserve keeps the same beat, but it only counts if your beast's Claw, Guarded Bite or Coordinated Strike did the work; a kinrath your beast never struck is just noise. Bring me back the Alpha Rhythm Tarn Hunt Tally from their nest; it's got the true count scratched into it somewhere under all that noise.

Take the key. The trail out the south side of these ruins drops into the Tarnished Jungles North; keep south into the Tarnished Jungles and the preserve gate is a short walk east, by a sealed passage. Go find the true count and bring it home.

A forced lead sets a rhythm the whole pack has to follow whether it wants to or not. The breeders goaded a kinrath into that place instead of letting one earn it. Sounds close to a real pack rhythm if you don't know better. It isn't. It's just noise wearing a beat's shape.
A true lead doesn't force tempo. It offers one, and the pack chooses to follow because the choice keeps everyone alive together. That's rhythm. Command without choice is just noise with good timing.

Every true count this preserve ever kept got scratched onto that tally. The breeders used it to fake a rhythm they never earned, and the Young Kinrath nest on it now. Bring it back and the true count's mine to read again, not theirs to counterfeit.
Six Young Kinrath still keeping that wrong beat. Your beast's Claw, Guarded Bite or Coordinated Strike on every one. Tally's still with them.
You're moving different. Steadier. Let me see what you brought back.
There's the true count, home again. Preserve's already sitting a little straighter for it. More noise further in, if you want to keep quieting it.

Five Pen-Scarred Kinrath past the young ones, deeper in, still dosed on the scent the breeders poured into the pens to force a tempo they couldn't refuse. That's not leading a pack. That's playing a drum nobody agreed to march to. Go put the five down with your beast's Claw, Guarded Bite or Coordinated Strike; any Pen-Scarred Kinrath counts. Bring me the Alpha Rhythm Beast-Pen Scent Vial from their pen.
Same gate, deeper in. Listen for the pens; you'll hear the wrong beat before you see them.

Dosed to force a tempo through scent alone, no choosing involved anywhere in it. Bring that vial back and I've got the forced beat isolated, proof of exactly how they've been playing this preserve like an instrument that never agreed to be played.

Earning a beat takes patience. Forcing one takes a vial and no conscience. They chose the vial because it's faster, and because a pack that's forced doesn't ask questions about who's leading it. Efficient. Also completely dishonest.

No. A pack under a forced tempo isn't moving together, it's just moving at the same time, which sounds the same for about a beat and a half before it falls apart. True rhythm holds because every beast in it is choosing the same beat freely. Force it, and the first missed step brings the whole line down.
Five Pen-Scarred Kinrath still forcing that beat. Bring the vial back.
You've got the rhythm of it now, I think. Let's hear what you brought.
Forced beat, isolated and dead. That's proof this preserve can use. You're keeping better time every visit.

Breeder's Iriaz Bull holds the deep pens, an iriaz bull the breeders set over the kinrath to force the beat on them. His rhythm's fast, and it's alone, and a single hunter just gets swept along by it instead of matching it. Bring two more hunters of your own; a pack answers a rhythm better than one dancer ever could. Put him down. Bring me the Alpha Rhythm Clawed Alpha Totem off his harness.
Same gate. Go together, and listen to each other as much as you listen to him. A pack that isn't syncing with itself won't sync against him either.

Fast, relentless, alone. He set that tempo honestly once, a young bull leading his own herd, before the breeders got their hands on him and taught him to force it on anything near. Half the beast I remember is still in that beat somewhere. The other half is exactly why you need company.

Alpha totem marks the true lead of a pack line, the one every follower chose freely. The breeders hung it on him clawed apart, because he never earned the lead; they forced it on him. Bring it back whole and the true lead is honored again.

One dancer against a fast solo rhythm just gets swept along, always a half-step behind, always reacting instead of matching. Three, moving together, and one of you can always be on his beat while the others answer from the gaps. That's not extra safety. That's the only way to actually keep time with something that fast.
Breeder's Iriaz Bull's beat is still fast, still alone. Gather your pack and answer it.
Your whole pack still moving. Good rhythm holds. Let me see the totem.
Whole. The true lead's honored again, first time in longer than this preserve's kept count. Rest your pack. The ones who carry his beat deepest are next, and they know it's coming.

Four left, the Elder Kinrath, in the deepest part of the preserve: the eldest kinrath, the first the breeders forced the wrong tempo into. Every pack since learned the beat from them. Bring your pack back in; four beats at once, out of sync with each other on purpose, is worse than one fast soloist. Put them down with your beast's Claw, Guarded Bite or Coordinated Strike; any Elder Kinrath counts. Bring me the Alpha Rhythm Preserve Keeper's Token from their nest.
Same gate, deepest part of the preserve. Four beats, deliberately out of sync with each other to confuse anyone listening. Keep your pack listening to each other first, them second.

Force instead of earn, drum instead of offer. Those four learned it so well they teach it to every pack hatched since. A pack built on that never actually moves together. It just moves at the same time, right up until it doesn't, and then it's four soloists standing where a pack used to be.

That token's the true count of who's allowed to call tempo for this whole preserve. The breeders took it when they ran and lost it in that nest when the packs turned. One real token in my hands, and every false beat they ever called gets silenced with it.

Because one hunter can only answer one beat at a time, and a rhythm this deliberately broken throws more beats at you than one hunter can track. A pack of your own splits the listening. Somebody's always got the next beat covered, even when it's coming from four directions at once.
Four kinrath, still playing their broken time. Bring the token back.
Whole pack, still together. Let's hear what you brought.
Whole. Their false beat's silenced for good. One rhythm left down there, and it's the one every other broken beat in this preserve got copied from. Your pack's ready for that one, I think.

Last rhythm. Old Iriaz Bull is the sire Breeder's Iriaz Bull learned his beat from. His tempo is seductive, and that's the danger of it: it sounds almost like a true lead's, close enough that a whole pack will follow it without noticing the wrongness until it's too late. Bring your whole pack. One hunter following that beat alone gets pulled all the way in before they know which rhythm they're keeping. There's no token this time. His rhythm breaking, for good, is the whole proof.
Then go, all together, same gate as always. Listen to each other first. His beat wants you listening only to him.

Because it's not a lie built from nothing. It's the true rhythm, the one I've spent my life teaching, bent just enough that it still sounds honest while it forces everyone near it to follow. You've been learning to offer a beat and let a pack choose it freely. He learned the same beat and decided choosing was optional. That's the whole difference, and it's the whole danger.

Because a soloist following a seductive rhythm alone has nothing to check it against, no second beat reminding them what true tempo actually feels like. A whole pack, playing their own honest rhythm together, gives each other something to hold onto when his beat tries to pull everyone into his time instead. That's not extra caution. That's the only defense a rhythm like his actually has an answer to.

Goes back to true tempo, offered and chosen, the way a pack's supposed to move. I'll be listening for it every day after this, and the day it sounds honest again all the way through, I'll know you finished the job right.
His beat's still playing, still seductive. Bring your whole pack when you go.
Quiet. Whole preserve's gone quiet, no beat at all, first time in longer than I've been listening. Tell me it's him.

Then the rhythm's true again, all the way through. That's Alpha Rhythm, finished: a beat offered, not forced, and a pack that chooses to follow because the choice keeps everyone alive together. You learned to hear it. Now go keep it. Your beast already knows the tempo. Trust it.
Back to the beat.
I'll quiet the six and bring the tally.
What do you mean, a wrong beat?
How does a lead beast set tempo for a pack?
What's this tally to your rhythm?
Let me listen a while longer.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Tarn Hunt Tally.
Back to the beat.
I'll quiet the five and bring the vial.
What's the vial doing to the tempo?
Why force a beat instead of earning one?
Can a pack even move honestly under a forced tempo?
Give me a little more time.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Beast-Pen Scent Vial.
Back to the beat.
I'll bring two more hunters and answer his beat together.
What's his rhythm like, exactly?
What does the alpha totem mean in your rhythm-language?
Why does one hunter fail against his tempo?
My pack isn't gathered yet.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Clawed Alpha Totem, whole.
Back to the beat.
We'll answer all four beats together.
What did the breeders teach them?
What does the keeper's token mean to your rhythm?
Why does breaking their rhythm take more than one hunter?
My pack needs rest first.
Here's the Alpha Rhythm Preserve Keeper's Token, whole.
Back to the beat.
Our whole pack, answering his beat together.
What makes his rhythm so seductive?
Why can't even a skilled soloist break it alone?
What happens to the preserve's rhythm, once he's gone?
Not until every one of us is ready.
It's done. His beat broke.
